title: Dog groomer or vet

fields.label: What you do
fields.help: Dog grooming (in a salon or a van), or a vet practice.

fields.label: Services and prices
fields.help: What you offer and the price for each size of dog (small, medium, large, giant), how long it takes and what's included. Extras and their prices.

fields.label: How a visit goes
fields.help: Drop-off to pick-up, or what happens at an appointment. What makes you different (one-to-one, no cages, fear-free).

fields.label: Times
fields.help: Drop-off or appointment times and days you're closed.

writerNotes: The hero follows one dog through a visit, drawn in profile. dog.kind groom for groomers: arrive shaggy and muddy, bath, dry, trim, finishing touches, ready. dog.kind vet for vets: arrive, weigh, look over (eyes, ears, teeth, heart, belly, joints), listen, vaccinate, all done. Give the dog a friendly name (the brief's own dog if it mentions one) and a natural coat colour; write the six stages for that visit with clock times.

tally: four numbers beside the visit. For groomers: coat length (cm or in) from long to short over the trim (stage 3), treats, minutes, tail wags at the end. For vets: weight first (its end is what the scale shows), checks done out of six, minutes, treats. Each with the stages it moves over (first, last).

prices.sizes: the brief's size bands (two to four) with a shape each (small, medium, large, giant). prices.services: up to three services with a price for every size exactly as the brief prices them (repeat a single price for each size), how long, up to four inclusions and an optional tag on the most booked. addons: extras with prices.
visit.steps: up to four steps of a visit; visit.promise: a short big mark (1:1, 0 cages, Fear free) and a sentence from the brief. Never invent accreditations or claims.
book: drop-off or appointment times (08:30), closed days (0 Sunday). The booking is a demo: nothing is booked.
hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop). theme.accent is the business's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
